name: HEARTS Capsule Hotel & Spa HAKATA
detail: Fukuoka Airport is close to Hakata Station, and the hotel is also near the station. There are pajamas and basic amenities provided, and the capsule is reasonably spacious with a TV, charging outlets, and a mirror, so it's comfortable. There are lockers for valuables, and it's convenient as you can access the hot spring bath from there. I enjoyed delicious bread at Dakomekka, which is very close to the hotel. The staff at the reception were friendly, and I felt safe staying in the women-only floor.

name: 9h nine hours Hakata station
detail: The Sleep Pod is specialized for sleeping. It's quiet and comfortable. I was impressed by the enveloping pillows. There is no TV or radio. There are USB and regular outlets available. It supports multiple languages, and the pictogram design is stylish. You can use a card key for both the elevator and lockers (the timing for scanning the locker QR code is a bit tricky). Organizing luggage in the lockers was somewhat difficult. You can eat and drink in the 9th-floor co-ed lounge. It's spacious, and of course, there’s free Wi-Fi, and a co-working space where you can work adequately. I opted for a breakfast included plan, which can be enjoyed at a fast-food restaurant behind the hotel. I chose a rice burger and miso soup. It was very delicious. Since each meal is over 1000 yen, the breakfast plan feels like a better deal. Amenities (toothbrushes and basic skincare products) are sold in vending machines within the hotel. There are several convenience stores nearby, so it was convenient. Very...

name: HEARTS Capsule Hotel & Spa Nakasu -Male only-
detail: I used it after a business dinner, and this is my second time. The bed is slightly wider than a typical capsule, and with clean sheets and a fluffy comforter, I was able to sleep comfortably. It’s just a minute from the station, with a convenience store and a beef bowl restaurant nearby, making it a very convenient hidden gem. I plan to use it again next time as well.

name: 9h nine hours Nakasukawabata Station
detail: It's convenient because it's directly connected to the subway, but when coming from the ground level, I found the signs inside Hakata Riverain to be unclear and I got lost. I received a large bag containing towels, a bath mat, loungewear, and disposable slippers, which made it easy to transport items from the locker to the capsule and then to the shower booth. In the evening, there was hair accumulated in the drain of the shower, but by early the next morning, it had been cleaned up nicely. The cleaning is thorough, and it has a sense of cleanliness. Since the capsule entrance is only separated by a roll screen, small sounds can be heard, so sensitive people may not be able to sleep well. Overall, I think I will use it again.

name: APA Hotel Fukuoka Tenjinnishi
detail: The location was easily accessible on foot and convenient for shopping. The accommodation had good hot water supply and the bathroom was clean, allowing for a pleasant stay. The housekeeping service was also very satisfactory. The staff's attitude was friendly, and the overall facilities were well-equipped, making for a comfortable time.

name: WELLCABIN TENJIN - Male Only
detail: Located just outside the bustling area of Tenjin, this capsule hotel is set in a quiet environment. It has a compact three-story structure and does not accommodate many guests. The exterior gives the impression of a converted fitness gym. The facilities include compact and simple shared toilets and washing areas (with dryers), shower rooms, and a coin laundry. Amenities, including towels and loungewear, are minimal, reflecting a cost-cutting approach. However, I felt that the cleaning and cleanliness were thoroughly maintained. During this visit, I stayed in a semi-private cabin for multiple nights. Despite the space being about 1.5 tatami mats, having a locker and a desk with a chair provided comfort, and being able to store belongings was very convenient. It was also nice to have the option to choose whether or not to have bed-making during consecutive nights. The only disappointing point was that the guest next door was making phone calls and crunching on snacks in their room, which is against the rules. If I had to wish for something more, it would be a large public bath and sauna, as well as another coin laundry, since there was only one on the first floor.

name: UNPLAN Fukuoka
detail: It was great to be right in front of exit 4 of Ohori Park Station, and there were nearby 24-hour ramen shops and convenience stores. The room was clean and there was ample space to store luggage and other items. Also, I used the restroom and shower facilities comfortably without any inconvenience. It was perfect for running in Ohori Park in the morning. The breakfast was simple but delicious. Although you could walk to Tenjin or Hakata for shopping, taking the subway is much more comfortable. Overall, I was more satisfied than with a typical capsule hotel!

name: The Millennials Fukuoka
detail: The room had one double bed with a reclining function, and it had a decent ceiling height as well as width. Despite being a capsule hotel, the space felt spacious. The facility was generally clean, and there was a complete separation of areas for men and women, with a security key system in place at the entrance door of the area, ensuring safety and security. There were free bar (free drink) sessions held twice, once in the evening and once at night. Despite being free, the staff made each drink individually, and they tasted quite sophisticated and delicious. I would definitely like to use this place again if the opportunity arises!

name: ZONK HOTEL Hakata
detail: There was a staff member who was either Korean or spoke Korean, and they were very kind. Other staff members were also able to communicate smoothly in English, and everyone provided very friendly guidance. Additionally, all the notices were also written in Korean, so it seems there wouldn't be a problem even if you can't speak English or Japanese. Storing luggage is 550 yen, which might seem a bit pricey, but it's cheaper than the lockers at Hakata Station, so it was fine. There's also a Lawson convenience store nearby. On the second floor at the front desk, beer, coffee, and water are provided for free and in unlimited quantities, and all the canned beers in the fridge within the accommodation are free, which is great. The check-in time is very strict, so if you arrive early, you can relax at the front desk, enjoy a beer, and have a light snack. The room is spacious enough to spread out your suitcase, and there's a full-length mirror, which is nice. The sound of the air purifier is a bit loud, but I found it okay as it served as white noise. The sink is also large, making it easy to do makeup.

name: APA Hotel Hakata Gion Ekimae
detail: 1. It was cheaper than other accommodations around, but maybe because it's vacation season, it felt expensive. 2. The staff were very kind. 3. It was convenient that they provided self check-in instructions in Korean. 4. It was good for security that you had to swipe the card to get on the elevator. 5. There's a Lawson convenience store right next to it and a FamilyMart across the street, making it convenient for snacks or water. 6. It is within walking distance from Hakata. 7. It is walkable to Canal Way and Nakasu. 8. It was perfect for solo stay. I could open my suitcase and use it comfortably. 9. The lobby is really cool. It's cool enough to make me happy, but it gets hot on the way to the room after taking the elevator [though it's not far, so it's manageable]. 10. I had to shower in the bathtub, but the shower curtain had a smell... However, it's manageable if you ventilate well. If I come to Fukuoka again, I would like to book this accommodation again if asked. 🫡🫡
